label: Thutmose I's pylons and obelisks
more: Thutmose I (reigned about 1504 to 1492 BC) built the Fourth and Fifth Pylons and a hall between them, and raised a pair of red granite obelisks before the Fourth Pylon, then the temple's west gate. One, about 21 metres tall, still stands. He was Hatshepsut's father.

label: Hatshepsut's obelisks raised
more: Hatshepsut raised two rose granite obelisks in Thutmose I's hall, in her year 16, about 1464 BC by Shaw's count (popular sources say about 1457 BC). Hers still stands, nearly 30 metres tall. Its pair fell, and its top was set upright by the lake in 2022.

label: Amenhotep III's Third Pylon and the scarab
more: Amenhotep III (reigned about 1390 to 1352 BC) tore down earlier monuments west of the Fourth Pylon and built the Third Pylon from their stones. His scarab stood at his temple across the Nile and was probably moved here by Taharqa, about 690 to 664 BC.

label: Granite sanctuary for Philip Arrhidaeus
more: After Alexander the Great died, his half-brother Philip Arrhidaeus was king in name. His name is on the granite shrine for Amun's boat, a copy of Thutmose III's, dated about 323 to 317 BC. One scholar suggests Nectanebo II made it and Philip only had it carved.
